title: Identification of Cell-Surface Proteins with Horseradish Peroxidase
author: Wu, Pandey, et al.
materials: Orbitrap Fusion Lumos Tribrid mass spectrometer

steps.title: Define biological replicate scheme
steps.instruction: Plan to generate four biological replicates for proteomic analysis, each replicate consisting of pooled striatal tissue from three mice.

steps.title: Prepare mouse batches for experiments
steps.instruction: Organize three batches of mice: Batch 1 – four animals for immunohistochemical HRP‑biotinylation validation (half labeled, half control); Batch 2 – four animals for streptavidin blot validation (half labeled, half control); Batch 3 – twenty‑four animals for proteomic analysis (twelve labeled, twelve control, pooled three‑mouse replicates).

steps.title: Acquire LC‑MS/MS data
steps.instruction: Run data‑dependent acquisition on a Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Fusion Lumos Tribrid mass spectrometer coupled to a Dionex UltiMate 3000 RPLC‑nano system to collect peptide spectra from each replicate.

steps.title: Process MS data with MaxQuant
steps.instruction: Analyze raw files in MaxQuant using the integrated Andromeda search engine against the Mus musculus Uniprot reference (UP000000589); allow up to two missed cleavages, set peptide and protein FDR to 1 %, enable label‑free quantification with a minimum ratio count of one, and use a parent ion tolerance of 20 ppm and fragment ion tolerance of 4.5 ppm.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of protein quantification
steps.instruction: Import MaxQuant output into R with the artMS package; apply global normalization across all runs using MSstats (median intensity equalization and Tukey’s median polish); censor missing values and retain only proteins detected in at least two of three biological replicates for a given condition.

steps.title: Perform STRING enrichment analysis
steps.instruction: Compare H₂O₂⁺ (HRP‑labeled) versus H₂O₂⁻ (non‑labeled) groups; identify proteins with log₂ fold‑change > 1 and p‑value < 0.05; submit these lists to the STRING database for cellular component (GO‑CC) enrichment of cell‑surface proteins (alternative tools: Enrichr, PANTHER may also be used).

steps.title: Annotate and classify enriched proteins
steps.instruction: Query UniProt for subcellular localization of each enriched protein; classify proteins annotated with plasma‑membrane, extracellular, cell‑surface, secreted, or synaptic membrane terms as CSPs, and those annotated only to nucleus, mitochondrion, or cytoplasm as non‑CSPs; optionally map cellular origin using publicly available scRNA‑seq datasets (e.g., Allen Institute striatal single‑cell data).

description: Astrocytes closely contact neurons and other cell types through complex membrane structures within their bushy morphologies.2 Molecular interactions at these cell–cell interfaces, mediated by CSPs, are essential for astrocytes to communicate with neighboring cells, particularly neurons, and to carry out their diverse functions.3,4,5 Recently advances in proximity-labeling based proteomics have enabled the profiling of CSPs with both cell-type specificity and spatial resolution.6,7,8 By genetically targeting horseradish peroxidase (HRP) to the cell-surface of striatal astrocytes, where the enzyme generates reactive radicals to covalently tag neighboring proteins with biotin that are in turn characterized by LC-MS/MS, we obtain rich putative cell-surface proteomes of striatal astrocytes. The protocol below describes specific steps for proteomic profiling of CSPs with HRP from striatal astrocytes. It can be readily adapted to profile CSPs from other cell types or brain regions by using AAVs driven by alternative cell type-specific promoters or by combining conditional AAVs with appropriate Cre driver mouse lines. In this protocol, we typically generate four biological replicates for proteomic analysis, with each replicate prepared from the striata of three mice. The procedure can be scaled to include additional samples or adapted to isolate CSPs from other cell types, provided that the appropriate mouse lines or AAV tools are available. We recommend preparing three batches of mice for the following steps. Batch 1: Four animals (four biological replicates) for immunohistochemical characterization of HRP biotinylation. For each animal, half of the tissue serves as the HRP-labeling group and the other half as the non-reaction control (omitting BxxP substrate or H2O2). Batch 2: Four animals (four biological replicates) for streptavidin blot validation of HRP biotinylation, processed in the same way as Batch 1 (half labeled, half control).
